completion:
Verify the performance of the fire-safety measures to the original design and to the existing standards.
3. Use fire-engineering techniques.

## Features of the obligation

Under the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005, the responsible person must keep records of fire safety arrangements, including details of fire and safety equipment, the actions taken after changes and the results of any risk assessments. The records must be kept for at least five years and made available to relevant stakeholders. In the case of a large risk assessment, records must be kept for the life span of the building.

The document must include the measures required to maintain and reduce the risk of fire, where appropriate.

The regulatory inspector (a local authority or police officer) has access, on specified conditions, to the risk assessment and relevant records. The performance of the building shall be verified and tested. The regulatory inspector should check that the risk assessment has been properly carried out
